resolution: Two predicates, never identified. Aristotle's self-mover (`SelfMovedIn`, Physics VIII.4) is a whole moved by itself, one part moving another; the prima via and STMT-NO-MOVER-MOVES-ITSELF-IN-ITS-RESPECT deny something else, that a thing is the mover of itself in the very respect in which it is moved (`MovesIn x x r`). VIII.5, 257b2-13 itself says a self-mover cannot move itself as a whole in the same respect, so the two are compatible. No inference passes from `SelfMovedIn x r` to `MovesIn x x r` or back: STMT-NATURAL-SELF-MOTION-HAS-A-MOVER says only that a self-motion has some mover in that respect.
